_comment: The acceptance gate's configuration (design §4, §7, §9). Copy it, set the worktrees and the out_dir, and commit the copy with the Day-1 lock.
Launch the runner from P_new's worktree: the plain-call arms run in-process under that worktree's code.
P_old: the commit after PR 2 and PR 3. P_new: PR 4b's head. P_unc: PR 5's head (drop the arm if PR 5 is not merged by Day 1; never add it mid-run).
The seed is fixed now; changing it after the lock is a new pre-registration.

Models: gpt-oss only (2026-10-04: Nemotron dropped from the experiments; about 14 tokens/s). A second model is added only if it passes the criteria fixed in the design (§7, D15), with its reasoning profile set before any run.

Judges (T5, decided 2026-10-04): Claude as an in-session subagent on Sonnet (never the model that wrote the rubrics), working only on the blinded export; Gemini 3.8 Flash over the API. Two labs, so their errors are independent. The API path (python -m experiments.judge calibrate) serves any judge given as a slug; the subagent path uses export-calibration and report-calibration.
prices: dollars per million tokens per model name, for cost per correct answer (§8.1, G5). Update from OpenRouter on Day 1 and freeze with the lock.

Interaction groups (design §6.6): P_rev (A, scripted reviewer), C0F (A and M, plain call plus follow-ups), P_M (M, category 10's script); P_unc+F joins when PR 5 lands. inrun_judges make the reviewer's and follow-up decisions during the run (API judges; the in-session subagent can't run headless). P_old branches into FB1 (EXECUTE at the parity floor; needs FA1 in P_old).
